title: Address healthcheck timeout + route reconciliation flakiness causing rollback failures during model rollouts
creator: Avery Park
summary: During a rolling canary swap for model v2.3 we observed intermittent rollback failures: the canary was marked unhealthy due to a downstream healthcheck timeout, the route reconciliation loop enqueued conflicting changes, and the automated rollback state machine failed to reach a stable state for several minutes. Users experienced elevated 5xx generation errors and latency spikes for affected tenants. This ticket tracks the post-incident analysis and implements fixes to make the rollback path deterministic and resilient to transient healthcheck timeouts.
timeline:
2026-03-09 09:45 UTC: Deploy started for v2.3 canary.
2026-03-09 09:52 UTC: First healthcheck timeouts observed on canary instances (p95 latency increase).
2026-03-09 09:55 UTC: Smart routing detected degraded canary and triggered rollback.
2026-03-09 09:56-10:02 UTC: Route reconciliation loop retried several times, occasionally re-routing a subset of traffic back to the canary due to race between reconciliation and healthcheck updates.
2026-03-09 10:03 UTC: Rollback state machine entered an error-retry loop and did not converge until an operator manually pinned the stable version at 10:07 UTC.
2026-03-09 10:15 UTC: Incident declared and mitigation completed.
2026-03-09 12:00 UTC: Post-incident ack and initial notes on Slack and incident channel.
impact: Affected approximately 12% of requests for customers on canary routing policies during the window. Observed 5xx rate spike up to 3.8% (baseline 0.1%) and tail latency p99 increase from 620ms to 1.9s for impacted routes. Two enterprise customers opened support tickets; no data loss reported but degraded availability for short period.
detection: Detected by automated SLO alert (route-error-rate > 0.5% for 5m) and on-call engineer flagged repeated rollback attempts via reconciliation logs. Dashboard: https://dashboards.internal.redwood/rollouts/ENG-20345. Incident channel: #inc-20345-rollout
root_cause: Three contributing factors: 1) healthcheck threshold and timeout values were too aggressive for the observed cold-start and upstream transient latencies, causing healthy but slow instances to be marked unhealthy; 2) the route reconciliation loop does not mesh safe-checks with the rollback state machine, allowing races where reconciliation re-applies canary routes while rollback is in progress; 3) rollback state machine lacked exponential backoff and idempotent guards, so transient failures produced retry storms that left the system in a non-convergent state.
corrective_actions: Short-term mitigations applied in incident: increased healthcheck timeout for canary group (from 500ms to 1200ms), manually pinned stable version for affected tenants, and temporarily disabled aggressive auto-reapply in reconciliation. Long-term fixes (tracked in action_items):
action_items: Implement reconciliation mutex: ensure route reconciliation honors active rollback locks (owner: Miguel Santos, estimate 3) - due 2026-03-20
Add exponential backoff and idempotency to rollback state machine to prevent retry storms (owner: Priya Nair, estimate 5) - due 2026-03-27
Introduce adaptive healthcheck per-model-profile: allow longer timeouts during cold-start windows and for large models (owner: Rafael Kim, estimate 3) - due 2026-03-25
Create automated test harness that simulates healthcheck timeouts + reconciliation races in CI (owner: SRE team, estimate 5) - due 2026-04-01
Update runbook: add explicit operator steps for manual pinning and safe rollback validation, plus a checklist for dependent services to check (owner: On-call rotation, estimate 2) - due 2026-03-18
Instrument more detailed rollback telemetry: add event IDs, transition reasons, and reconciliation conflict counters to the rollout traces (owner: Observability team, estimate 3) - due 2026-03-22
decisions: We will not revert the v2.3 model rollout; instead we will harden the rollout machinery. Default healthcheck timeouts will be increased for canaries of models >2B params and adaptive behavior will be enabled. Rollback orchestration changes will be released behind a feature flag and toggled on after verification in a staging environment.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Increasing healthcheck timeouts decreases sensitivity to real failures and could delay detection of genuine instance crashes. To mitigate, adaptive healthchecks are targeted to known cold-start windows and accompanied by liveness checks. Introducing reconciliation mutexes increases complexity in distributed state management; we'll keep changes minimal and reversible and add extensive integration tests.
follow_up_notes: SRE to run a controlled canary in staging with injected healthcheck latency to validate the new mutex and rollback backoff logic. Schedule a review with customer success for affected accounts to confirm no lingering issues. Track metrics for two weeks post-deploy: route_error_rate, rollback_convergence_time, reconciliation_conflict_count.
postmortem_summary: The incident revealed an operational race between healthchecks, route reconciliation, and the rollback state machine. Fixes combine configuration changes (adaptive healthchecks) with control-plane logic hardening (reconciliation mutexes and rollback idempotency). We prioritized fixes that reduce false-positive unhealthy marks while preventing non-convergent rollback behavior. Action items are assigned and scheduled across rollout, SRE, and observability teams.
verification_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests for rollback idempotency and reconciliation mutex. 2) Staging canary with artificial healthcheck delay to simulate cold-start. 3) Gradual rollout of orchestration changes behind feature flag with monitoring alerts to auto-disable if rollback_convergence_time regresses. Verification owner: Miguel Santos - complete by 2026-03-27.
